subject.title: Provider key pools + bucket-aware cooldown/backoff on 429 (Gemini projects) to prevent retry storms

question: Should OpenClaw make Gemini/project quota-bucket key pools a native provider/auth routing contract, or keep bucket-aware key rotation outside core until a plugin/provider seam can own it?
rationale: This choice changes public config, persisted auth state, provider fallback semantics, key-secret handling, status output, and upgrade expectations; automation should not invent those boundaries.

options.title: Add Native Pool Contract
options.body: Define a minimal opt-in core/provider contract for key buckets and cooldown state, preserving current key rotation and auth-profile defaults while adding Gemini project grouping.

options.title: Fold Into Provider-Profile Routing
options.body: Keep this issue as a phased child of the broader provider-profile routing design and require bucket metadata to land only after the generic pool contract is approved.

options.title: Defer To External Sidecar Or Plugin
options.body: Document the current sidecar/plugin path and do not add native bucket-aware key routing until maintainers decide the core state/config cost is justified.

recommendation.title: Add Native Pool Contract
recommendation.body: Define a minimal opt-in core/provider contract for key buckets and cooldown state, preserving current key rotation and auth-profile defaults while adding Gemini project grouping.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans generic provider API-key rotation, auth-profile storage/order, and public configuration boundaries where steipete has the strongest current history signal.
